For the appellants : Ms. Sunita Sharma, Sr. Advocate with Mr. Dhananjay Sharma,
Advocate, for the appellants in RFA No.122 of 2017 and for respondents No.1 to 3 in RFA No.76 of 2018.
For the respondents : Mr. Vivek Negi, Advocate, for the appellants in RFA No.76 of 2018 and for respondents No.2 & Mr. Pranay Pratap Singh, Additional Advocate General, for the respondents/ State.

M.S. Ramachandra Rao, Chief Justice.
.

These two appeals are filed under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (in short "the Act") challenging the judgment dt. 18.03.2017 passed in LAKH Petition no.01-LAKH/4 of 2013 of the learned District Judge, Sirmour at Nahan, Himachal Pradesh.
2) The appellants in RFA no.122 of 2017 are the claimants whose land has been acquired under the said Act through a Notification issued under Section 4 of the Act on 18.11.2008.
They shall be henceforth referred to as "Claimants".

Yogeshwar Singh & Others vs State Of Himachal Pradesh & Others on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136334240/

sentences.text: The HPPCL was the beneficiary for whom the said land alongwith other land had been acquired under the said Notification.
It shall be henceforth referred to as "the Beneficiary".

4) In that Notification, admittedly, the extent of land owned by the claimants was shown as 46-14 bighas in Khasra no.591/480, situated in Mauza Deed Baggad, Sub Tehsil Dadahu, Tehsil Nahan, District Sirmour, H.P.
The Award of the Land Acquisition Collector 5) Subsequently, Award no.653 dt. 06.08.2012, was passed by the Collector Land Acquisition, HPPCL, Uttam Bhawan, Shimla-4.

In the said Award , he granted compensation @ Rs.65,000/- per bigha, but stated as under:-
"The area of khasra number 591/480 as per the dimensions recorded on the map is much less than 46-14 bigha which is recorded in the revenue record.
This error was detected by the revenue officials while doing enumeration of trees on the spot.
The error therefore requires to be rectified/clarified from the revenue authorities before making the payment of excess area.
The case for ascertaining the actual area of this khasra number will be submitted to the District Collector, Sirmour.

The payment of compensation of this khasra .
number will be made strictly in accordance with the dimension on the map.
The payment of doubtful area will be made after ascertaining the factual report from the revenue authority.
The compensation shall be disbursed to the persons interested as per their share recorded in the record of rights and Award statement.
Payment in case of dispute shall be mad either after the settlement of such dispute or shall be deposited in the court of Ld. District Judge in case the dispute is referred to the Ld. Court."
The Reference Court's judgment 6) Challenging this Award, the claimants sought a reference under Section 18 of the Act, which was numbered as LAKH Petition no.01-LAKH/4 of 2013.

7) The said reference was initially disposed of on 07.07.2015 , but the claimants appealed against it to this Court, and the matter was remitted back to the Court of District Judge, Sirmour at Nahan, by this Court on 09.09.2016, with a direction to permit the claimants to lead their evidence and then to disposed it off.

entities.text: Court of District Judge, Sirmour at Nahan
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
8) The Reference Court framed the following issues:
"1. Whether the Collector has not properly assessed the compensation of the acquired land and the same is liable to be enhanced, as alleged?

OPP Yogeshwar Singh & Others vs State Of Himachal Pradesh & Others on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136334240/
2 2.

entities.text: OPP Yogeshwar Singh & Others vs State Of Himachal Pradesh & Others on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation in respect of the entire land of khasra No.591/480, measuring 46-14 bighas, as alleged?
OPP 3.
Whether the reference petition is barred by limitation, as alleged?OPR 4. Relief."

9) The claimants examined PW-1 & PW-2 and marked Ex.PW-1/A to Ex.P-8.
10) The State/ Benficiary (HPPCL) filed Ex.RA dt. 04.07.2015, copy of a Sale .
Deed and Ex.R-1 to Ex.R-5.
11) The Reference Court enhanced the compensation to Rs.1 lakh per bigha from Rs.60,500/- per bigha which had been given by the Land Acquisition Collector, on the basis of an Award previously passed by the same Court in Reference Petition no.3-LAKH/4 of 2013, titled as Rikhi Ram & others vs. Principal Secretary & others, on 16.06.2015.
12)

entities.text: Rikhi Ram & others vs. Principal Secretary & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As regards the extent of land which is said to be available in Khasra no.591/480, which was also in dispute, the claimants' led evidence in that regard and contended that their land which was acquired was of extent 46-14 bighas and that the exact area had been mentioned in the declaration issued under Section 6 of the Act.

13) They contended that the area shown in the Jamabandi was 46-14 bighas and the area was not shown to be 22-5 bighas as was being contended by the State/ HPPCL and that the Award has been passed for the total extent of 46- 14 bighas.
14) They also stated that they had filed a Civil Suit for correction of the area, but the suit was dismissed.
15) To rebut the evidence of the claimants, the State/HPPCL did not tender any evidence as regards the extent of land of the claimants which was acquired.

16) However, the Reference Court did not give any finding as to extent of land .
owned by the claimants.
RFA no.122 of 2017 and RFA no.76 of 2018 17) Contending that the extent of their land which was acquired is 46-14 bighas

;
that compensation at the rate of Rs.13 lakhs per bigha ought to have been granted instead of Rs.1 lakh per bigha, keeping in mind the potential for tourism, residential and commercial purpose of the land in question, the claimants filed RFA no.122 of 2017 before this Court.

Yogeshwar Singh & Others vs State Of Himachal Pradesh & Others on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136334240/

entities.text: Yogeshwar Singh & Others vs State Of Himachal Pradesh & Others on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The State/HPPCL has filed RFA no.76 of 2018, stating that the Reference Court had failed to return any specific finding with respect to possession of the acquired land and the increase in the compensation to Rs.1 lakh per bigha by the Reference Court is not valid in law.
19) Counsel for both the parties reiterated their respective contentions.
They also contended that the said judgment has been challenged in the Supreme Court of India and the SLP also came to be dismissed.

. 
21) The counsel for the beneficiaries did not dispute these facts.
Consideration by the Court 22)

If the land covered by the same Notification issued on 18.11.2008 under Section 4(1) of the Act and also covered by the same Award dt. 06.08.2012 was subject matter of the said RFA. No.360 of 2018, we are of the opinion that the claimants herein are also entitled to fixation of market value of their acquired land as Rs.7 lakhs per bigha and therefore the compensation granted by the Reference Court is liable to be enhanced from Rs.1 lakh per bigha to Rs.7 lakhs per bigha,
irrespective of its classification & category and that interest & all statutory benefits as per law are also required to be paid to the claimants.

23) As regards the question as to what was the actual land in Khasra no.591/480 belonging to claimants which was acquired is concerned, i.e. whether it was 46-14 bighas ( as is contended by claimants) or whether it was 22-5 bighas (as is being contended by the beneficiary HPPCL/State),
we may point out that such a dispute was noticed even in the Award passed on 06.08.2012 by the Land Acquisition Collector, but he had not decided the said issue and left it open to be decided by the Revenue officials and he had granted compensation for only 22-5 bighas of land instead of 46-14 bighas.

24) Before the Reference Court, PW-2 the Tehsildar, admitted that the Notification under Section 4 of the Act and the declaration under Section 6 thereof mentioned the extent of land of the claimants which was acquired to .
be 46.14 bighas.
This was also reflected in a Jamabandi and report under Section 8 (Ex.P-5).

He also admitted that the acquisition area had not been de-notified by the State.
Yogeshwar Singh & Others vs State Of Himachal Pradesh & Others on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136334240/
4

entities.text: Yogeshwar Singh & Others vs State Of Himachal Pradesh & Others on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 25 ) Though, in cross-examination, he did say that the Naib Tehsildar Dadahu, gave a report of the extent being only 22-15 bighas, admittedly, it is not the case of the beneficiary that any such report was prepared after notice to the claimants.
Therefore, such a report is not binding on the claimants.
26) To rebut the evidence of PW-2, admittedly, the State/beneficiary did not adduce any evidence that the extent was not 46-14 bighas but only 22-5 bighas.

27) In this Court, the State/beneficiary had filed CMP no.5308 of 2022 in RFA no.76 of 2018, under Order 41 Rule 27 CPC, to place on record certain documents to prove the measurement of the land in question.

28) No valid reason is assigned by the State/ HPPCL as to why this material was not adduced either before the Reference Court or before the Land Acquisition Collector where the matter had been pending since 2008.

29) In our opinion, once a declaration is issued under Section 6 of the Act that a particular parcel of land is required for a public purpose, Section 6(3) of the Act gives a finality to the said declaration by stating that that the said declaration shall be conclusive evidence that the said parcel of land is needed for a public purpose.

30) Since it is not in dispute that in the instant case the declaration under Section .
6 of the Act, specifically mentioned 46-14 bighas as the land belonging to the claimants which was acquired, there is no question of the State/ HPPCL leading any evidence to disprove the same in view of Section 6(3) of the Act.
31) Therefore, CMP no.5308 of 2022 in RFA no.76 of 2018, is dismissed.

32) We may also point out that the dismissal of the Civil Suit no.43/1 of 2013 filed by the claimants before the Civil Judge (Jr. Division), Nahan, District Sirmour, H.P., for a declaration that the extent of land which is acquired in Khasra no.591/480 is 46-14 bighas, is not relevant for the reason that at Para- 27 of it's judgment, the Civil Court gave a finding that during the pendency of the Reference Petition under Section 18 of the Act before the District Judge, it had no jurisdiction to entertain such a suit.

entities.text: Civil Judge (Jr. Division), Nahan, District Sirmour, H.P.
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: So finding , if any, regarding the extent of land was given in such a judgment rendered by the Court having no jurisdiction, will not bind the parties.

33) Therefore, we hold that the extent of the land of the claimants, which is acquired, is 46-14 bighas and they shall be entitled to compensation for the same on market value at the rate of Rs.7 lakhs per bigha with interest and all statutory benefits under the law, as mentioned above.
34) Accordingly, RFA no.122 of 2017 is allowed, as above, and RFA no.76 of 2018 is dismissed.
